objective: Improve the chance that all three selected fixtures have the correct unique first score. Keep every original R7 first, ordered trio, WDL, and real-line decision. Compare the three fixtures selected by two specified ranking rules across each competition's complete slate.
panel: Use the original R7 main/forecasts.jsonl.gz for all 20 competitions in configs/analysis-scope.json. Per competition train only on evaluation rows strictly earlier than its earliest recent target, and evaluate once on all recent rows. Never borrow training fixtures across competitions. Retain scopes without recent fixtures with zero denominators. Historical slates use the original recorded fixture date as provided; where it is unzoned its conversion to Beijing time is unknown. Prospective slates use the declared Asia/Shanghai date and are labelled separately.
inputs: Use only the original R7 candidate first-score probability p, probability mass of the ordered trio t, and the three WDL probabilities. Further inputs are the R7 first score, R6 first and market first as actually available at that origin. Features in order are (t-p-0.20)/0.15, (WDL probability of the outcome implied by that first-0.40)/0.25, indicator that the first is a draw minus 0.5, R6 first agreement centred on 0.5 (zero if missing), and market first agreement centred on 0.5 (zero if missing). Clip each component to [-2,2]. Inference accepts only these selected values and has no result-derived fields. Never use p_observed or actual ranks as features.
fit: For each competition use the logit of the raw first-score probability, clipped strictly inside [1e-6,1-1e-6], as a fixed offset. Add an intercept and the five listed features. Fit Bernoulli negative log likelihood for the original unique first being correct, plus 0.5 times 16 times the sum of squared coefficients including intercept. Optimise in float64 via L-BFGS-B with coefficients bounded to [-2,2], no tuned hyperparameters. Fewer than 50 prior observations or only one outcome class yields six zero coefficients and an explicit fallback. No target-period refit. Fixed before running the new ranking, with previously published overall R7 scores already known.
assessment: Within each competition and original date, rank by either raw p or calibrated probability descending, ties by original ID. Keep three fixtures or all on a shorter day. Report full three-first sweeps per complete batch, sweeps per all batches, picked primary and ordered-trio hits per seat, scheduled versus filled slots, short batches, switched identities, paired sweep gains/losses on identical complete dates and a 95% paired date bootstrap (2000 resamples, seed 20261125). Repeat the original four KPI counts on the full same-fixture population and cite same-fixture market coverage. Do not tune on the recent window or present retrospective selection as prospective certification.
forward: Use the signed R7 192-fixture registration. Use the fitted weights if available; refit with all verified retrospective R7 rows strictly preceding the whole prospective freeze date, with the same estimator. Only whole registered competition/Beijing-date slates whose earliest match has not begun are eligible; preserve already-started dates as excluded and retain all short slates. Lock a separate research ranking and both rules before the first included kickoff with original R7 issue hashes and ordered firsts. This research ranking cannot substitute for the original J1, AFC or other user-facing selections.
